subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should cron tool restrictions become a new `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` config surface, inherit from `tools.subagents.tools`, or stay limited to per-job `payload.toolsAllow`?
rationale: The implementation changes public config and a security boundary, and the wrong default could either leave scheduled jobs over-permissive or break existing cron jobs during upgrade.

options.title: Add explicit cron policy
options.body: Add `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with documented precedence against existing policy layers and per-job `toolsAllow`, then test embedded and CLI-backed cron behavior.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Treat isolated cron sessions as delegated execution for tool-policy purposes, with docs explaining that `tools.subagents.tools` also governs cron jobs.

options.title: Keep per-job only
options.body: Do not add a global config surface; instead document `payload.toolsAllow` and add runtime safeguards only for duplicate announce/message delivery.

recommendation.title: Add explicit cron policy
recommendation.body: Add `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with documented precedence against existing policy layers and per-job `toolsAllow`, then test embedded and CLI-backed cron behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The current schema and cron/gateway policy history points most strongly to steipete, and the open decision is config/security policy rather than a narrow runtime patch.
